items.title: Luis Conte interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 24, 2025
items.q: Those guys were friends with my dad. They’re all from Santiago. And these guys would come in the house and they would have these parties

ctx.x: Was there a point that you can think of that you decided that you were going to become a professional musician? Was it gradual or was there like a turning point?

It was – well I have to explain to you because I never thought I was going to be a musician. I’m a really late guy. A super late guy. I played music since I was a little boy. I played guitar also, I had lots of guitar lessons when I was in Cuba. I was able to learn how to play son and some things like that from traditional – yeah, a wonderful teacher. And I had conga, bongo, I didn’t have timbales, but guiro, maracas, I had everything. And I would play. And sometimes my parents would have parties and you know,…

figure this, man. This is a 15-year-old just detached from his world, in Hollywood. You know I’m just, I don't know, I was lost. I didn’t know what I was doing I was just floating around. I wanted to finish high school then I guess you’ve got to go to college. I don’t have any money so I can’t go to an expensive college, I just go to a city college. And I still wasn’t thinking of being a musician. I didn’t know what I was going to do.
